newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria plans oil refinery maintenance in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria plans oil refinery maintenance in 1997.

text.p: Nigeria's oil refineries at Port Harcourt and Kaduna are to undergo overdue turnaround maintenance during 1997, the managing director of Port Harcourt refinery said.

Mansur Ahmed told Reuters on Wednesday that Kaduna would be closed for maintenance at some time during the first or second quarter of the year, while Port Harcourt's New Refinery would be closed in the last quarter of 1997.
"Funding constraints have made turnaround maintenance impossible this year and it is long overdue, but we cannot close two refineries at the same time," Ahmed said.
The northern Kaduna refinery is running at 70,000 barrels per day (bpd) from a capacity of 110,000 bpd.
Southeastern Port Harcourt's New Refinery is running at 105,000 bpd from a possible 150,000 bpd.
Port Harcourt's 60,000 bpd Old Refinery is not currently operating.
"We hope to find a window of opportunity during 1997 to restart the Old Refinery," said Ahmed.
Nigeria's other refinery at Warri on which no maintenance is not planned for next year is running at 75,000 bpd from a possible 125,000 bpd.

The state-run refineries have suffered from years of insufficient investment to keep them at capacity and despite producing around two million bpd of crude oil Nigeria is often forced to resort to fuel imports to meet local needs.
